attacks.claim: createShareLink embeds the owner's project API key in the share URL query string, and the share page loader returns it to every viewer as replayKey. Anyone with the link gets a working credential for the owner's project. Deleting the share does not revoke the key.

The key in the URL leaks through access logs, Referer headers, browser history, and Slack/X unfurl crawlers. The logging redaction covers only the Authorization header, so a query-string key is not redacted.
attacks.evidence: Gateway access logs redact the `Authorization` header ... Share pages are server-rendered with Open Graph tags so links unfurl nicely on Slack/X.

attacks.claim: Anonymous viewers replay against the owner's project quota. For pro projects that is per-token billing across all models ('*'), so any link holder can drive unbounded spend on a paying customer's account.
attacks.evidence: Viewers without an account replay against the owner's project quota. / pro: models: ["*"] ... daily_tokens: null

attacks.claim: The $4k/month hard budget is not enforced anywhere. The free pool can autoscale to 24 H100s, which is about $43k/month at $2.49/h. Signup needs no card, so per-account limits multiply with the number of accounts.
The public rate limit (20 per minute) does not match the shipped config (20 per second, burst 40), which is 60x looser. Staging QA used per: minute, so the production config was never tested.
attacks.evidence: rate_limit: { requests: 20, per: second, burst: 40 } / (staging config used `per: minute`)

attacks.claim: The changelog promises a 100k tokens/day cap, but the free tier config has no daily_tokens key, and no enforcement path is shown. Token spend per account is effectively bounded only by max_tokens_per_request and the rate limit.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: daily_tokens in the free tier block; changelog says "100k tokens per day"

attacks.claim: The budget math leaves no headroom. Two replicas at $2.49/h come to about $3.6k/month, roughly 90% of the budget, before any autoscaling. The <30% utilization claim has no benchmark behind it.
attacks.evidence: Two H100 replicas serve the projected free load at < 30% utilization; ... ~$3.6k/month

attacks.claim: The alert pages on-call when the free pool exceeds 6 replicas, but the pool is configured to autoscale to 24. Launch-day scaling will page continuously, which is noise. There is also no alert on spend or budget.
attacks.evidence: Alerting: free pool replicas > 6 pages on-call

attacks.claim: Rollback only stops new signups. Shares already distributed with embedded keys keep working, and no key rotation or share invalidation path is described. The public announcement cannot be recalled.
attacks.evidence: Rollback: `free_signup_open` off stops new signups; existing free keys keep working.

attacks.claim: Shared conversations are publicly readable with no expiry, no access control, and no warning or redaction step. Messages may contain personal data, and OG tags may expose it in previews.
attacks.evidence: Anyone with the link can view the conversation and re-run it, even without a Lumen account.

attacks.claim: No load or spike test is described ahead of an HN/X launch. QA is functional only, so behaviour at a multiple of the projected 3,000 DAU is unknown.
attacks.evidence: QA summary (staging) lists only functional checks

attacks.claim: The claim that free traffic cannot degrade paid latency is supported only by GPU pool isolation. The shared gateway fleet and the share-replay path against pro projects are not isolated.
attacks.evidence: Free pool is isolated from `shared-h100`, so free traffic cannot degrade paid latency.

attacks.claim: The free tier limit (20/s, burst 40, about 1,200/min) is higher than the pro tier (600/min, burst 120), so free users get more throughput than paying customers. This is likely a config error.
attacks.evidence: free: { requests: 20, per: second, burst: 40 } vs pro: { requests: 600, per: minute, burst: 120 }

attacks.claim: Public user-generated share links launch with no stated moderation or takedown process beyond owner deletion.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: ToS update, abuse/takedown policy for public shares

attacks.claim: The new GET /v1/usage endpoint has no stated auth scope or rate limit.
attacks.evidence: New `GET /v1/usage` endpoint returns your current daily token usage.

attacks.claim: All capacity depends on a single GPU provider at on-demand pricing, with no fallback described.
attacks.evidence: the GPU provider's on-demand rate of $2.49/h
